findings.claim: Acceptance criterion 5.1 (validate and archive the OpenSpec change, then write the execute handoff retaining stale-registry and historical-projection risks with next command `/kbd-new-phase kbd-control-plane-recovery`) is not satisfied: the criterion is still marked `[ ]` and the diff contains no openspec archive or handoff artifacts.
findings.evidence: acceptance_criteria section 5: `- [ ] 5.1 Validate and archive the OpenSpec change, then write an execute handoff...` — the only unchecked criterion, and no diff hunk touches `openspec/` or any handoff file.
findings.suggested_fix: Complete the archival + handoff step (or split it into an explicit follow-up change) before this change is treated as done; per the constraints, archiving requires the QA gate to pass.

findings.claim: An explicitly configured `SOVEREIGN_SYNC_SOCKET` is silently ignored whenever the socket file does not exist at that instant (e.g. during a supervised launchd restart), downgrading the transport to TCP `http://127.0.0.1:7892`, which the managed daemon does not serve — the opposite of what the operator configured.
findings.evidence: `default_target()`: `let socket = std::env::var_os("SOVEREIGN_SYNC_SOCKET")...; if let Some(socket) = socket.filter(|path| is_socket(path)) { return Target::Unix(socket); }` then unconditionally `Target::Http("http://127.0.0.1:7892".into())`. The removed comment in kbd.rs confirms the managed daemon does not listen on TCP: "TCP :7892 exists only when it is started with an explicit --tcp, which the managed LaunchAgent does not pass."
findings.suggested_fix: When `SOVEREIGN_SYNC_SOCKET` is set, always select `Target::Unix` and let the connect failure surface as `TransportFailure::Unreachable` (which already triggers the local-commit fallback in `submit_fresh`); only apply the `is_socket` existence filter to the discovered default path.

findings.claim: If the managed key file `~/.config/sovereign-sync/device-key.json` exists but is corrupt or unreadable, `device_signer()` now hard-fails instead of falling back to the platform credential store, introducing a new total-signing-outage mode in a change whose stated purpose is KBD availability.
findings.evidence: New hunk: `if let Some(path) = managed_device_key_path().filter(|path| path.is_file()) { return load_device_key(&path); }` — the `?` inside `load_device_key` (`serde_json::from_reader(File::open(path)?)?`) propagates any IO/parse error, and the `match self.key_storage { ... PlatformCredentialStore => self.platform_device_signer() }` fallback below is never reached on error.
findings.suggested_fix: On `load_device_key` failure for the discovered managed path, log a warning and fall through to `self.platform_device_signer()` (or at least make the error message explicitly name the managed path and the recovery action of deleting/fixing it).

findings.claim: The Unix-socket response body is collected with no size bound (`response.into_body().collect().await`), so a malfunctioning local daemon can make the CLI buffer unbounded memory within the 30s timeout window.
findings.evidence: `request_unix`: `.collect().await.map_err(...)?.to_bytes()` with no `content-length` sanity check or cap, unlike any size-limited decode elsewhere in the client.
findings.suggested_fix: Cap the collected body (e.g. check `content-length` header and/or abort collection past a few MB) before `to_bytes()`.
